phase11.auditSummary: docs/PHASE11_AUDIT.md. Phase 10 closed green and was re-measured at entry (301 unit tests, verify OK, 28 captures, zero console errors). The headline audit finding is that there was no client performance problem: no scene implements update(), nothing allocates per frame, rendering is event-driven (renderAll runs per interaction, not per frame), and the drag handler does a setPosition plus a linear scan over ~25 drop zones with no validation or re-render per pointer move. The crowded-table capture already held 58 fps. One real inefficiency existed - renderAll analyzed every meld twice per human-turn render, once via invalidMelds() and again via canConfirm(). The genuine findings were resilience, not performance: three separate ways the game fails on a browser with storage blocked or an asset step that throws, and one online path that could lock input forever. Slop was near zero - no TODOs, no commented-out code, no duplicated implementations, two dead exports.
blockers: RESOLVED S1: loadSave() read localStorage unguarded and settings.ts calls it at module scope, so a browser that throws on storage access (Safari with site data blocked, webviews with storage disabled) failed to boot at all - blank canvas. Reads now go through safeGet(), and the localStorage default parameter is resolved lazily inside a try because reading the property itself throws before any guard in the body could run.

RESOLVED S2: src/net/client.ts touched sessionStorage unguarded inside ws.onopen, ws.onclose, ws.onmessage and leaveRoom. A throw inside a socket callback aborts it: the reconnect handshake would never send, and the retry-vs-terminal decision would be skipped, leaving the UI on a dead socket with no notice. All four sites now route through readToken/writeToken/clearToken.

RESOLVED S3: BootScene.finish() was async, called without await from both branches, with no error handling. A throw from loadPixelFont() or composeCardFaces() was an unhandled rejection and scene.start('menu') never ran - permanent black screen, despite the procedural fallbacks that make the game fully playable without composed card faces. The fallible part is now caught, the failure is recorded in debugApi.errors rather than swallowed, and the menu always starts.

RESOLVED S4: onlinePending locked all input from FEITO/COMPRAR submit and was cleared only by state_sync or proposal_rejected. A dropped or ignored proposal on a still-open socket produced neither and there was no timeout, so the player was left with a dead board and no explanation. Set/clear now goes through a single setOnlinePending() helper that owns a 10s ONLINE_PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS timer; on expiry the lock releases, the resyncing notice shows, a resync is requested, and the scene re-renders (without that re-render the board stays visibly dead, since the message that would normally trigger the next render is the one that never came).

Two further gaps: the invalid-meld reason was reachable only by hover (unusable on touch, and the objective copy literally said "passe o mouse no ✗"), and the FEITO strip collapsed every invalid meld to a generic phase message even though the exact reason was already computed.
phase12.decision: The brief asked for bounce/restore on an invalid drop. Mexe Mode is built on temporarily invalid drafts — rearranging the table means passing through states the validator rejects — so bouncing every rule-invalid drop would remove rearranging entirely. Decision: the drop is still accepted and the meld still draws invalid; what changed is that the player sees red BEFORE letting go. Bounce stays reserved for drops the editor genuinely refuses (tutorial gate, table card that may not return to hand). Illegality is communicated by the helper, never enforced by it; the FEITO gate is untouched, so no helper can allow an illegal confirm.
delivered: src/table/snap.ts — pure snap-target model. computeSnapTargets(draft, card, config) returns one target per meld plus the new-meld target, each with status legal/incomplete/illegal, the validator reason, a display-sorted preview of the resulting meld, and joker assignments. Three statuses, not a boolean: a meld under 3 cards is a normal mid-edit state, not an error. Calls analyzeMeld/sortMeldCards — never re-derives a rule.
GameScene drag highlights coloured by status: solid green legal, soft gold incomplete, dashed red illegal (shape channel, not hue alone). Targets computed once on dragstart, never per pointer move.

Non-mutating ghost preview panel on drag-over: the resulting meld as small cards in resulting order, a joker hint taken only from the model assignments and only when legal, and one status line. Cleared on drag leave, dragend and at the top of renderAll.

phase14.perfNote: The zoomed table is fill-rate bound: it draws the same ~57 cards at card scale 1.0 instead of stress-table's ~0.45, roughly 5x the pixels each. CI runs on a GPU-less container that rasterizes in software, so table-zoomed reads 27 fps there against 52 on a GPU-backed machine, while stress-table clears 50 on the same runner because its cards are small. One genuine inefficiency was found and fixed along the way - the table mask was applied per object (hundreds of stencil passes, sprite batching broken) and is now applied once to a container, worth +5 fps on CI. Off-screen row culling was added too, but measured as a no-op on the current fixture (content 136 units vs a 102-unit viewport, only 1.33x), so it is protection for larger tables rather than a fix for this number. The table-zoomed floor was then set from measurement at 20; stress-table keeps >=50 to guard the normal unzoomed path.

phase17.auditSummary: docs/PHASE17_REAL_DEVICE_AUDIT.md. Entry state re-measured, not assumed: 454/454 unit green at 08a82a1. Phases 13-16 had already landed safe-area insets, viewport-fit=cover, the two authored worlds, 44px touch floors, card-layer pointercancel, connectivity handling and the stamped service worker, so the audit confirmed those and found four genuine gaps: no app sleep/resume handling anywhere, leaked audio-unlock listeners with no pause/resume, missing pointercancel on the two UI panels, and no battery/quality setting. Unlike Phase 16 this pass also ran on a real iOS Simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.4, real Mobile Safari), which found two further defects that Playwright emulation had never surfaced.

realDeviceFindings: BLOCKER, found only on real iOS: the landscape win screen ran its 3-button stack past the 270-unit world bottom, so MENU was cut off and unreachable, and the per-player stats line rendered underneath MESMA PARTIDA. Root cause was one bug, not two — buttonY0 was capped at a hardcoded vy(225) that never accounted for the height of the button stack itself, so the stack overflowed and any content taller than the cap kept flowing under it. First fix attempt anchored the buttons correctly but left the stats line still overlapping; the second added the fit ladder and was confirmed against pixels (ios/26-win-landscape-fixed2.png).

HIGH: cold boot showed a black screen with zero feedback for 12-27s on the simulator (ios/01-menu-portrait.png at 12s, menu up by ~27s). Warm reloads are sub-second. Fixed with the static boot indicator.

CONFIRMED GOOD on real iOS: portrait and landscape menu/game/mexe/settings/win all render correctly; nothing sits under the Dynamic Island or home indicator in either orientation; the new 14-row settings panel fits at ROW_PITCH 17 including at textscale=125; orientation change mid-match preserved hand, score and turn across both rotations.

Not supported by the code: GameScene carries localSeat, a single-point onlinePending input lock with a timeout, revision-ordered view reconciliation and a resync path, and OnlineScene.canAct() gates the lobby separately.
